about: An expense tracker: note what money was spent on and how much, on the diary's day page as it happens or later from the plugin's own page, optionally with a category; then see each month's total, a twelve-month column chart, a per-category breakdown and a calendar shaded by spending. Each expense keeps its own currency (by default whichever was used last, or a fixed one chosen in Settings; synced across devices). The page shows everything combined in one currency of the user's choosing, converted at downloaded exchange rates, and can instead show each currency separately, unconverted. The export never converts. These strings are fetched only once the user enables the plugin, and are merged into the app's main bundle under the `plugins.expenses.` prefix — a key written here as "title" is referenced in code as plugins.expenses.title.
tone: Same as the main app: plain, calm, second person, no exclamation marks. Above all non-judgemental — this is a diary noting where money went, not a budgeting app. Never imply that spending is good or bad, too much or too little: no "only", "just", "too", "overspent", "saved" or anything that reads as praise or a warning. Amounts are facts, stated as such.

expenses.where: A card on the diary's day page below the composer — always on today, on a past day only if something was recorded then (otherwise a single small "add an expense for this day" button), never on a future day; the plugin's own page at /plugins/expenses, with a month switcher, three summary figures, a twelve-month column chart, a per-category bar list and that month's expenses grouped by day; a categories dialog and add/edit dialogs opened from that page; a synced settings card holding the default currency (a fixed one, or whatever was used last); a tab on the Calendar page shading each day by how much was spent; the Markdown export; and a three-screen tour opened from the Plugins list in Settings.

keys.name: The plugin's name in the Plugins list in Settings and on its Calendar tab. A noun, not a sentence.
keys.description: One line under the name in the Plugins list, explaining what enabling it does.
keys.title: Heading of the day card, the plugin page and the Markdown export section. Usually identical to `name`.
keys.addForgotten: A small, quiet button shown on a past day that has no expenses yet, in place of the whole card. Pressing it opens the card, unlocked, to add something remembered late. Should not sound like a reminder or a reproach.
keys.dayTotal: Screen-reader-only prefix read before the day's total(s) in the card header. The visible text is just the amount(s).
keys.nothingThatDay: Shown on a past day's card, locked, after its last expense was deleted during the same visit.
keys.saveFailed: Error toast when a write fails.
keys.deleted: Toast after deleting an expense. It carries an Undo button (common.undo).
keys.editExpense: Accessible name of an expense row, which is a button that opens it for editing. {{name}} is the description (or category name) and {{amount}} the formatted amount.
keys.unlock: Accessible name of the padlock on a past day's card while locked. An action.
keys.lock: The same button once unlocked, offering to lock it again.
keys.dayLockedPast: Tooltip on the padlock while locked: why editing is blocked and what tapping does.
keys.dayUnlockedHint: Tooltip on the padlock once unlocked.
keys.amountLabel: Accessible name of the amount field.
keys.amountInvalid: Shown under the form while the amount field holds something that can't be read as an amount. Gentle — it is a typo, not an error the user should feel bad about.
keys.currencyLabel: Accessible name of the small currency button inside the amount field. {{currency}} is the currency's full name, already localised ("Euro").
keys.searchCurrency: Placeholder of the search box in the currency list.
keys.descriptionLabel: Accessible name of the description field.
keys.descriptionPlaceholder: Placeholder of the description field. Says it's optional; only the amount is required.
keys.categoryLabel: Accessible name of the category picker.
keys.uncategorized: The picker's "no category" option, and the label shown for expenses filed under none.
keys.category: The nine starter categories. Short, everyday nouns for where money goes; users can rename any of them. `groceries` is food and household basics bought to take home; `eatingOut` is cafés, restaurants, takeaway; `bills` is utilities, subscriptions, rent-like recurring payments; `leisure` is going out, hobbies, entertainment; `shopping` is clothes and other goods.
keys.categoriesButton: Button in the plugin page header opening the categories dialog. Hidden visually on narrow screens (icon only), but still read out.
keys.categoriesDescription: Under that title. Explains renaming and retiring, and that retiring doesn't change past expenses.
keys.newCategoryPlaceholder: Placeholder and accessible name of the field for adding a new category.
keys.renameCategory: Accessible name of a category's name field in the dialog. {{name}} is its current name.
keys.retireCategory: Tooltip and accessible name of the button that hides a category from the picker. Used for starters, and for custom categories that already have expenses; those are retired rather than deleted so past expenses keep their name.
keys.deleteCategory: The same button on a custom category no expense uses yet: it deletes the category outright (with an Undo), since there is no history to keep.
keys.categoryDeleted: Toast after that deletion, with an Undo button. {{name}} is the category's name.
keys.restoreCategory: The same button on a retired category, bringing it back.
keys.retiredCategories: Small heading above the retired categories in the dialog.
keys.categoryRecord: How a category row is described in the backup-import review. {{name}} is the category's name.
keys.addExpense: Button in the plugin page header and empty state, and the title of the dialog it opens.
keys.addExpenseDescription: Under that dialog's title: which days can be picked.
keys.editTitle: Title of the dialog for editing an expense from the plugin page.
keys.dateLabel: Label of the date field in the add dialog.
keys.empty: The plugin page's empty state heading. Matter-of-fact.
keys.emptyPageDescription: Second line of the empty state: the two places an expense can be added.
keys.previousMonth: Accessible name of the month switcher's back arrow.
keys.nextMonth: Accessible name of its forward arrow.
keys.currencySwitcher: Accessible name of the currency tabs, shown only when more than one currency has been used and the page is set to show them separately.
keys.viewSwitcher: Accessible name of a two-option switch on the plugin page, shown when more than one currency has been used: show everything combined in one currency, or each currency separately.
keys.viewCombined: That switch's first option: every expense converted into one currency and added together. Short — it sits beside a currency code.
keys.viewSeparate: Its second option: one currency at a time, nothing converted.
keys.displayCurrencyLabel: Accessible name of the button showing which currency combined totals are in (its visible text is just the code, e.g. EUR); pressing it opens the currency list. {{currency}} is the currency's full name, already localised.
keys.approximately: Marks an amount as converted between currencies, so approximate: a day's combined total, and the converted figure under an expense paid in another currency. Keep the ≈ sign; {{amount}} is already formatted with its symbol.
keys.ratesTitle: Heading of a collapsible card at the bottom of the plugin page: a small currency converter and the rates of the user's currencies. Only shown while the rates are under a week old.
keys.ratesAmount: Accessible name of the converter's amount field.
keys.ratesFrom: Accessible name of the converter's source-currency button (visible text is the code). {{currency}} is the full name, localised.
keys.ratesTo: The same for the target currency.
keys.ratesSwap: Accessible name of the button between them that swaps the two currencies.
keys.ratesPair: One exchange rate, e.g. "$1.00 = €0.80". {{from}} and {{to}} are formatted amounts; usually only the order or spacing needs adapting.
keys.ratesUnavailable: Shown in the converter when the source has no rate for one of the two currencies.
keys.ratesCompareWith: Text before a currency button above a list of the user's own currencies in the rates card: the list compares them with whichever currency that button shows.
keys.ratesReference: Accessible name of that button (visible text is the code). {{currency}} is the full name, localised.
keys.ratesDirection: Accessible name of a two-option switch beside it choosing which way round the list reads.
keys.ratesEachIn: First option: each row shows what one unit of the user's currency is worth in {{currency}} (an ISO code), e.g. "$1 = €0.86". Very short.
keys.ratesOneIn: Second option: each row shows what one {{currency}} is worth in that row's currency, e.g. "€1 = $1.16". Very short.
keys.ratesNothingToCompare: Shown instead of the list when the only currency the user has used is the one picked to compare with.
keys.ratesSource: Small print at the bottom of the card: the rates' publication date ({{date}}, formatted), the source's name (keep "currency-api" as is), and that they are indicative, not what a bank would charge.
keys.ratesNote: A small line above the figures when some amounts were converted. {{date}} is the date the exchange rates were published, already formatted. Neutral, informative.
keys.ratesStale: Replaces ratesNote, as a warning, when those rates are more than a week old. Says how old, what that means for the totals, and that they refresh by themselves when the device is online — no action asked of the user.
keys.ratesMissing: Shown when some currency has no exchange rate at all, so its expenses are listed but not counted in any total. {{currencies}} is a comma-separated list of ISO codes; the plural follows how many currencies there are.
keys.monthTotal: Label under the month's total. The month itself is named just above, so this is short: literally "this month" even when browsing an older one reads fine in context, but a translation may prefer a neutral "total".
keys.dailyAverage: Label under the month's average spend per day. {{count}} is how many days that average is over: days the plugin was switched on, plus any day with an expense recorded, up to today. Days it was off with nothing recorded are left out, so a month it was only on for a week reads as an average over a week.
keys.expenseCountLabel: Label under the number of expenses recorded that month.
keys.lastTwelveMonths: Caption above the twelve-month column chart.
keys.monthSoFar: Caption above the area chart of the picked month's running total, day by day.
keys.spentThatDay: Part of the readout beside that caption, for the hovered (or latest) day: what was spent on that day alone. {{amount}} is formatted. Shown after the running total and the date, separated by middle dots.
keys.monthSoFarTotal: Screen-reader-only caption of the table behind that chart. {{amount}} is the month's total so far.
keys.runningTotalColumn: Screen-reader-only column header in that table: the cumulative total up to that day.
keys.nothingThisMonth: Shown in place of the category bars for a month with nothing recorded.
keys.listFilterLabel: Text before a dropdown above the month's list of expenses; the dropdown's value (a category name, or allCategories) completes the phrase.
keys.allCategories: The dropdown's default option: the list is not filtered.
keys.calendarLabel: Calendar tooltip for a day with expenses. {{amounts}} is one or more formatted totals (one per currency, already joined); {{count}} is how many expenses.
keys.settingsTitle: Heading of the plugin's settings card.
keys.settingsDescription: Under that heading. Unlike the other plugins' cards (device-only reminders) this setting follows the account, and says so.
keys.defaultCurrencyDescription: Under it: it only pre-selects, and each expense can still use another currency.
keys.currencyLastUsed: The default-currency setting's first and default option: new expenses start in whichever currency was used for the last one. Same idea and tone as the entry importance setting's "Whatever I used last".
keys.exportDayTotal: Heads the expenses block under a day in the Markdown export, with that day's total interpolated. A day that mixed currencies gets each total in turn, joined with ·, since this plugin never converts between them. Keep the colon: the lines beneath it are a list it introduces.
keys.exportNoteHeading: A `##` heading in the export's preamble, above exportNote. These exports are read by an AI agent, so the document explains every notation before using it — this is the expenses half of that, beside the diary's own notes on tags and importance.
keys.exportNote: One paragraph telling the reader how to parse an expense line. The `- <amount>: <description> (<category>)` fragment is the literal shape of the output: translate the words inside the angle brackets, and leave the backticks, the colon, the hyphen and the round brackets exactly as they are in every language — they are punctuation the parser sees, not prose.
keys.exportByMonth: A `###` heading over the export's closing table, which totals categories (rows) against months (columns).
keys.exportCurrenciesSeparate: Sits above that table when more than one currency is in play, explaining why there is one table per currency instead of one total. Omitted entirely when only one currency was used.
keys.exportTotal: Both the last column's header and the last row's label in that table — the same word has to serve for a row total and a column total, so prefer the noun that works for both.
keys.onboarding: The tour's three screens: `day` (a live copy of the day card), `stats` (the page's figures and charts over a made-up year) and `calendar` (the calendar tab). Each has a `title` and a one- or two-sentence `lede`. `previewNote` sits under the live previews. `day.demoCoffee` and `day.demoGroceries` are the descriptions of the two made-up expenses on the demo card — ordinary, everyday purchases.
keys.changeIcon: Accessible name and tooltip of the round icon at the start of a category's row in the categories dialog, which opens the icon picker. {{name}} is the category's name.
keys.iconFor: Title of the icon picker when opened for a category. {{name}} is its name.
keys.newCategoryIcon: Accessible name of the icon button beside the "new category" field, and the icon picker's title when opened from it.

languageNotes.en: Reference language; source strings are authored here.
languageNotes.es: Tú, not usted, matching the rest of the app. "Gasto" for an expense; "importe" for an amount.
languageNotes.it: Tu, not Lei, matching the rest of the app.
languageNotes.ja: です・ます, matching the rest of the app. Only the unsuffixed `calendarLabel`/`dailyAverage` keys are needed — Japanese has a single plural category.
languageNotes.zh: Simplified Chinese, matching the rest of the app. Only the unsuffixed `calendarLabel`/`dailyAverage` keys are needed — Chinese has a single plural category.
